lifecycleFollowup.exactBehavior: Coordinate existing import/export managers with actual workers across processes sharing a store. A crash-safe edit request pauses new work and stops active work at import seed/export query/copy boundaries. An activity lease delays private draft acquisition until the active worker commits, then excludes workers through all owned child closures and manager Apply/Cancel. The existing manager window polls asynchronously with exact reference wait messages and supports Cancel/window close. User pause settings stay intact, including later changes by a separate live consumer. Actual CLI scheduler rests wake on acquire/release; successful import manager Apply separately resets the due cache, while Cancel/failed saves do not publish that notification. Stale unlocked files never pause workers. Both schedulers retain a marker captured before worker execution through their subsequent wait, so manager completion between work and rest cannot lose its notification. An already observed active request retains bounded retry rest.
limits: Native file-lock requests replace Qt global running flags and transient Boolean overwrites. The native manager has a cancellable waiting state, whereas the reference publishes a non-cancellable wait job. Scheduler wakeups poll at one-second intervals rather than Qt publications.
An individual import, file copy or database query finishes before the next safe boundary. Filesystem marker modification times are wakeup hints; live OS leases determine whether work may run.
